newsitem.title: USA: Late spot Midwest US propane gains on EIA report.
newsitem.headline: Late spot Midwest US propane gains on EIA report.

text.p: Spot Midwest U.S. propane prices jumped sharply late Wednesday immediately after release of new EIA data showing a further 1.5 million barrel draw on already low stocks in the region, players said.
"Prices are coming back up because of the EIAs," one Midwest player said, noting prices had soared to a seven-year high of $1.00 a gallon Tuesday on bullish API data.
But they eased back down to 92 cents by early Wednesday afternoon as buyers vanished in wait of the EIA report.
It showed Midwest stocks of 15.2 million barrels, about six million below the same time last year.
A 5,000-barrel Conway parcel was sold for 98 cents a gallon soon after the EIA report was issued at 1700 EST (2200 GMT), with offers returning to late-Tuesday levels of $1.00 or more.

The EIA report showed East Coast and Gulf Coast stocks little changed from the prior week, with the Midwest draw pushing U.S. stocks 1.6 million barrels lower to a total of 44.8 million -- below the historical norm.
"During November, U.S. inventories fell by nearly 5.0 million barrels, their steepest November decline since 1992," the federal agency added.

Conway prices jumped an electrifying 15 cents a gallon on Tuesday, traders said, on the heels of new American Petroleum Institute data showing a large stock drawdown in the nation's heartland during the month of October.

Traders said the monthly API report, released late Monday, estimated Midwest stocks by late October had fallen over 3.5 million barrels from late September -- leaving only about 12.5 million left in primary storage.
Spot propane, meanwhile, in the Gulf Coast trading hub of Mont Belvieu, Texas, was offered at 69.25 cents late Wednesday before the EIA data came out, about 1.75 cent weaker than Tuesday prices.
Belvieu prices had risen 1.50 cents on Tuesday in sympathy with Conway's blustering strength.
-- Ransdell Pierson, New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1632
